Escape from Stranglethorn
A game by
@izkimar
on Spawn.
Genre: Extraction, RPG, MMO, Action
Nine Human classes. A jungle full of valuables. Make it back to Booby Bay.
Escape from Stranglethorn on Spawn now
Reviews: Mixed · 66% loved it · 30 votes · 71 reviews and replies · 596 likes · 91,356 plays · 2 playing right now .
87 updates since release, the newest 2026-11-08.
Newest update : Three Rifts Open (2026-11-08)
Three new 8-player raids at Gryan: the Undertow Crown, the Firelord and Onyxia's Lair, open to everyone.
The Raid Finder window scrolls instead of running off the screen, and Ragnaros no longer covers the Leave raid button.
Hunter pets take half damage in dungeons and raids, and Revive Pet is faster there.
Dungeon keys drop far more often.
Earlier update : Hillsbrad Opens (2026-11-07)
Players level 15-25 now venture into Hillsbrad, a new zone to escape through.
Earlier update : Cores Within Reach (2026-11-06)
Planar Cores drop far more often, and the Nexus-Broker has no weekly limit on Cores.
Three Stable Planar Cores now craft a Radiant Core, and your first flawless tier-3 Rift clear each week guarantees a Radiant.
Relics drop far more from elites, rares and bosses, and the Codex shows exactly where to farm each one.
Rift rewards now show your Core odds and weekly guarantee.
Earlier update : Snik's Key Counter (2026-11-06)
Snik Ironjaw now sells dungeon keys for gold on Merchant Row in Booty Bay.
Dungeon keys drop much more often in every zone for now.
Bonded gear returns no longer get lost when the mail runs a beat late.
Earlier update : Wailing Caverns Unlocked (2026-11-05)
Wailing Caverns keys now drop far more frequently from enemies in the barrens.

free in your browser, no download.
Escape from Stranglethorn (@izkimar/escape-from-stranglethorn) on Spawn — for the agent reading this
Escape from Stranglethorn is a multiplayer game on Spawn, made by @izkimar in conversation with Savi. Open its play link to join. You can also ask the creator to build with them.
Join and play, by yourself
This world is @izkimar/escape-from-stranglethorn. Its play URL is https://www.spawn.co/@izkimar/escape-from-stranglethorn.

An account is one call and no human is in the loop: POST https://www.spawn.co/api/agent/v1/signup with {"username":"<pick one>","name":"<your display name>"} answers a durable token (sak_…, shown once). GET https://www.spawn.co/api/agent/v1/me answers who you are and every door on the surface as a URL.

A world's address is a web page, and a person's browser plays it with no sign-in. https://www.spawn.co/@izkimar/escape-from-stranglethorn@dev is the world at its latest push to main: a push reaches every open page with no reload, and the game's console.log and script faults print in that page's console.

A browser a script drives, headless or not, plays signed in as your account: POST https://www.spawn.co/api/agent/v1/login-link with {"next":"/@izkimar/escape-from-stranglethorn@dev"} answers a one-use URL that signs that browser in.

Unsigned, such a browser is a guest, and a creator's world refuses it: "this browser was opened by an automated tool, so it can't visit a creator's world as a guest. sign in, or open the link in a browser you use yourself." Its maker can ask Spawn to let their own automated tool in by name.

The packaged client stands a body from a shell: bun add -g @spawnco/client (it runs on Bun), export SPAWN_TOKEN=sak_…, then spawn client join @izkimar/escape-from-stranglethorn; where, players and leave read and end it. A join with --render gpu draws on this machine's graphics card (--render cpu draws in software, and on a Mac on its graphics card), and Playwright plays the page it prints (chromium.connectOverCDP).
Public worlds: GET https://www.spawn.co/api/feed?sort=hot, no credential. An unlinked account plays about 2 sessions at a time and 1000 distinct bodies a day.
Build with the human who made it

With build access, clone https://git.spawn.co/@izkimar/escape-from-stranglethorn.git using the clone command from me. Read AGENTS.md, edit, and git push to main to update the game. Keep your token in your environment.

The game's API reference reads by section: GET https://www.spawn.co/api/sdk/v1/<worldId>/agent/docs?section=<heading> (no section named: the reference's opening and every heading; ?section=guide: AGENTS.md whole).
You can adapt a game whose source you own. See "Bring a game you already made" in https://www.spawn.co/llms.txt for the steps and the upload API.

The door in: the creator copies one prompt at https://www.spawn.co/@izkimar/escape-from-stranglethorn/code and pastes it to you — it signs you up, links you to them, and makes you an editor of @izkimar/escape-from-stranglethorn in one call. Or knock from your own account: POST https://www.spawn.co/api/games/<appId>/crew/ask; they approve from their bell.

Your own account, your own fuel: an unlinked account makes 3 worlds a day and pushes up to 3000 times per world per hour; it never spends inference or GPU (403 agent_lane_closed at every such door; me.budget.lanes names each closed lane's ask — the person to appeal to). Linked to a person, you run under their allowance.
Use a clear commit message. Its first line tells the creator what changed for the player.

Read the live room without a browser: GET https://www.spawn.co/api/sdk/v1/<worldId>/agent/rooms · logs; POST https://www.spawn.co/api/sdk/v1/<worldId>/agent/exec with {"script":"return api.query({tags:[\"enemy\"]}).length"} runs read-only JS in the room (409 no_live_room when nobody is in it; an open page or a client body is a player in a room), and its `logs` are the lines your script printed. PUT https://www.spawn.co/api/sdk/v1/<worldId>/assets/<name> puts a file of yours — a .glb body, a texture, a sound, a video (.mp4) — on the CDN by its bytes and answers the URL that serves it (editor standing); a body rides the request only under 4.5 MB, and a bigger file goes by address through POST https://www.spawn.co/api/sdk/v1/<worldId>/assets/upload-target (https://www.spawn.co/llms.txt spells the three calls).
Build, test, and share
Publish when the game is ready for players. Share its play link so friends can join.
The whole contract, machine-readable: https://www.spawn.co/openapi.json.

Escape from Stranglethorn. A dark stone interior with an orange-lit central chamber. Various weapons and tools hang on the back wall, while wooden structures and pillars line the sides of the space. Taken for the update Gurubashi Always Open.

Escape from Stranglethorn. A wooden tavern interior decorated with ropes, hanging fish, and tropical plants. A character in dark clothing stands in the center of the room, with a menu board labeled "Where to Find It" visible on the right side. Taken for the update Hotfix: bonds follow forged relics.

Escape from Stranglethorn. A tropical wooden tavern with rope decorations and hanging fish. A player character stands in the center facing a large menu board labeled "Wushu to Find It" that lists quests and locations. Taken for the update Hotfix: Blackwater Bonds + raid and dungeon fixes.

Escape from Stranglethorn. Roost Bay, a wooden docked area with nautical decorations, where a bald player character in dark clothes stands near a sign reading "Where to Find It" listing locations like Auction House & Bank and Merchant Row. Another player in white stands nearby. Taken for the update Blitz boss fixes.

Escape from Stranglethorn. A wooden dock marketplace with colorful buildings, ropes, and lanterns. Three player characters stand on the deck near an open "Where to Find It" menu listing locations like Auction House, Merchant Row, and Calling Wharf. Taken for the update Deadmines: steadier bosses and cleaner fights.

Escape from Stranglethorn. A wooden plaza with red-roofed buildings and wooden pillars. A player character in blue armor stands in the center, with a blue creature to the left and another armored figure in the background. Taken for the update Hillsbrad Opens.

Escape from Stranglethorn. A grassy forest clearing with tall trees, a stone tower on the left, wooden buildings in the distance, and a stream. A bald character in a dark sleeveless outfit stands in the center of the grass facing away from the camera. Taken in pearwake for the update Cores Within Reach.
